prompt_text: Who does backflow testing and repair near Liberty MO?
answer_verbatim:
Do you need residential or commercial service? I can either give specific local company names (I don’t have live web access so I’d need you to let me look them up), or I can give a quick ready-made plan to find a qualified tester plus phone/email templates and the questions to ask. Which would you prefer?

Meanwhile, here are immediate, practical steps so you can get service today:

1. Contact the City of Liberty (Liberty Utilities / Public Works) first
   - They can tell you city requirements, approved tester list (if any), and where to submit test reports.

2. Search for certified backflow testers near Liberty, MO
   - Use search queries: “backflow testing Liberty MO”, “backflow tester near Liberty MO”, or “RPZ tester Kansas City area”.
   - Good places to look: local plumbing companies, irrigation/sprinkler companies, fire-protection contractors, and plumbing franchises (Roto-Rooter, Mr. Rooter, etc.). Many irrigation companies also do backflow tests.

3. What to verify when you call
   - Certification: tester must be certified to test backflow assemblies (look for ASSE/AWWA backflow tester certification or state-certified backflow tester).
   - Experience with the specific assembly type you have (RPZ, double-check, reduced pressure, etc.).
   - They will provide a written test report — confirm they will file or give you the report in the format required by Liberty.
   - Insurance and bonding.
   - Ask whether they do repairs on-site and whether they will submit the repaired test results to the city.

4. Typical cost ranges (ballpark)
   - Residential simple assemblies: ~$75–$150 per test.
   - Commercial or complex assemblies/repairs: $150–$400+ depending on parts and complexity.
   - Always get a written estimate for repairs.

5. Useful resources to verify certification or find testers
   - City of Liberty Public Works / Utilities (ask for cross-connection/backflow program).
   - Missouri Department of Natural Resources or state plumbing board (may list certified testers).
   - American Backflow Prevention Association (ABPA) — directory and guidance.

If you want, tell me:
- residential vs commercial,
- your address or zip (Liberty is 64068/64069 area codes) — I can then produce a short list of nearby companies you can call (you’ll need to confirm current availability), or I can write a ready-to-use phone script/email and a checklist to evaluate quotes. Which would you like?
